panels.description: THE THREE PHASES ARE PLOTTED SEPARATELY AND MUST NEVER BE AGGREGATED HERE. A single total series is the cheapest thing to build and would foreclose the phase-triage runbook scenario operations writes in story 8: ADR-0036 §11 decomposes the forward path into three phases precisely because they have DIFFERENT REMEDIES, and an undifferentiated total does not tell an operator which to pursue. The story-8 latency alert gets a scenario of its own and is never folded into egress exhaustion. Per-phase remedies are NOT restated here - see docs/observability/metrics/mh-service.md §Media Forward Path, and the Media Forward Latency by Phase panel on the Media Handler - SLOs dashboard. THE 'total' PHASE IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from this panel by selector. It exists to carry the ADR-0011 objective, because quantiles do not sum and the SLO number needs its own observation; an operator who reads the total first cannot tell which of three remedies to pursue. AND THERE IS NO SERIES MEASURING THE SLI-ELIGIBLE SPAN TODAY. The eligible subset is receive_buffer + processing (MH-internal, not client-influenceable); 'total' is wider and IS client-influenced, because it includes transmit_buffer, which is slow-subscriber time. But the eligible subset is VISIBLE here, not AVAILABLE: p95(receive_buffer + processing) cannot be constructed from p95(receive_buffer) and p95(processing), by the same quantiles-do-not-sum property that justifies 'total' existing at all. So do NOT ratify an objective off these two series - the quantity cannot be computed from what is plotted. A series for the eligible span would only exist if a LATER story narrows the Total phase's recording to end at egress-enqueue; that is an MH hot-path change and this story does not make it. See docs/observability/slos.md §Open: the target. SAMPLED ONE-IN-N: read the sample-ratio panel on the SLOs dashboard before reading any rate off _count. This panel is the phase-triage substrate; the SLOs dashboard carries the objective view.

panels.description: Frames MH discarded on the publisher-to-relay side, broken out by reason - the WHY behind the Media Frame Drops by Direction panel on the Media Handler - Overview dashboard, which answers only WHETHER and on which side. AN EMPTY PANEL MEANS NO DROPS OCCURRED, AND THAT IS THE EXPECTED HEALTHY STATE OF THE LOOPBACK. A Prometheus counter materialises no series until it is first incremented, so 'No data' here is the normal reading, not a broken pipeline. There is deliberately no 'or vector(0)' in this query: it would fabricate a series and flatten the by-reason breakdown that triage depends on. TWO REASONS ARE DECLARED BUT CANNOT FIRE TODAY AND ARE NOT LIVE DETECTORS: partial_frame_discard (unreachable until video - audio is one frame per datagram, so the stream-carried path has no producer) and stream_rate_limited (unreachable until uni-streams/video, for the same reason - MH opens no uni-streams this story). A permanently flat series for either is correct, not a fault; do not go looking for a bug behind it. A FLAT PANEL IS AMBIGUOUS AND ALWAYS WILL BE: this family reads present-and-flat-at-zero both when the handler is idle and when no media session ever started, and the two are byte-identical here. Discriminate with Media Session Starts by Outcome first, then with mh_media_frames_dropped_total{reason="transport_receive_dropped"} - flat means no datagram ever arrived, moving means MH received them and never read them. Counted as increase() rather than rate() per ADR-0029 Category A: at the deployed 15s scrape cadence a single drop under rate() renders ~0.003/s, which reads IDENTICAL TO HEALTHY on the one panel whose purpose is that a single drop is visible. The reason vocabulary and its direction mapping are NOT restated here - see docs/observability/metrics/mh-service.md §Media Forward Path.
panels.title: Ingress Drops by Reason

panels.description: Drops on the two reasons whose contract is that they READ ZERO FOREVER: transport_send_refused (the transport seam refused a datagram it should have accepted) and relay_rewrite_failed (rewrite failed on a frame that had already decoded cleanly - an MH bug, never a sender fault). Any non-zero value is an invariant violation, not load shedding. This panel reads 0 rather than 'No data' when nothing has been counted (noValue), because for an invariant the distinction between 'no series yet' and 'zero violations' is not one an operator should have to make. That is why noValue is set HERE and not on the by-reason breakdown panels, where an empty panel is itself the signal. Deliberately NOT the shape of the alert rule that watches this family: this is increase() over the dashboard range, not a rate over a fixed window. Do not copy it into a rule or a rule into it.
panels.title: Zero-Forever Invariant Drops

panels.description: The fraction of egress attempts the transport accepted, built on the ATTEMPTS SUM (forwarded + dropped) rather than on one addend - a frame count cannot be denominated by anything else, and building on forwarded alone silently rises when drops rise. Expression source: docs/observability/metrics/mh-service.md §Media Forward Path, which is where it is derived and explained; it is reproduced rather than re-derived here. Reads empty in a healthy idle loopback for the same reason the drop panels do - no egress attempts, no series. That is not a delivery failure. key_custody=operator: MH cannot read the media it forwards; MC can. A keyless relay working correctly - drops at zero, delivery ratio at 1 - is NOT end-to-end and NOT zero-trust (ADR-0036 §4).
panels.title: Egress Delivery Ratio

title: Media Handler - Media Path
description: MH media-path triage board: where an operator answers WHY, after mh-overview has answered WHETHER. key_custody=operator - media is encrypted between clients; MH, transport and storage cannot read it; MC can. That is accepted operator custody, NOT end-to-end and NOT zero-trust.
